keywords.def: a situation where prices rise far above real value and then suddenly collapse.
excitement that makes something seem more important or valuable than it really is.
an estimate of how much a company or asset is worth.
investing or making decisions based on guesses about the future rather than solid evidence.
when something is priced much higher than its true or real value.
a person or organisation that puts money into something hoping to make a profit.
a sudden and dramatic fall in prices or value.

sentences.en: Artificial intelligence is everywhere right now.
sentences.zh: 人工智能现在无处不在。

sentences.en: We use it to write emails, generate images, recommend videos, and even help study English.
sentences.zh: 我们用它来写电子邮件、生成图片、推荐视频，甚至用来辅助学习英语。

sentences.en: Some people believe AI will completely change the world, just like the internet did.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为人工智能将彻底改变世界，就像互联网曾经做的那样。

sentences.en: Others are more sceptical and worry that the excitement has gone too far.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则更加持怀疑态度，担心这种狂热已经走得太远了。

sentences.en: Every day on the news, we hear about new AI startups worth billions of dollars, governments investing huge amounts of money, and tech companies racing to become the next AI leader.
sentences.zh: 每天在新闻中，我们都能听到价值数十亿美元的新AI初创公司、政府巨额投资，以及科技公司争当下一个AI领头羊的消息。

sentences.en: There is a lot of optimism, but also a lot of hype.
sentences.zh: 这里面有很高的乐观情绪，但也充满了过度的炒作。

sentences.en: Some people are starting to question whether we are we seeing real, long-term growth, or are we living through an AI bubble?
sentences.zh: 有些人开始质疑，我们究竟是在见证真实、长期的增长，还是正身处于一个AI泡沫之中？

sentences.en: In today’s episode of Thinking in English, we’ll explore what an economic bubble really is, look at famous bubbles from history, and ask whether artificial intelligence is following the same pattern or whether this time is different.
sentences.zh: 在今天的Thinking in English节目中，我们将探讨经济泡沫究竟是什么，回顾历史上的著名泡沫，并探讨人工智能是会遵循同样的规律，还是这一次有所不同。

sentences.en: At the same time, we’ll learn some useful English vocabulary!
sentences.zh: 同时，我们还将学习一些实用的英语词汇！

sentences.en: Artificial intelligence, or AI, is changing the world very quickly.
sentences.zh: 人工智能，也就是AI，正在以极快的速度改变世界。

sentences.en: You have definitely heard of tools like ChatGPT or Google Gemini.
sentences.zh: 你一定听说过像ChatGPT或Google Gemini这样的工具。

sentences.en: They can write emails for you, generate example questions for an IELTS test, and instantly process long articles into bullet points.
sentences.zh: 它们可以为你写邮件、为雅思考试生成样题，还能瞬间将长篇文章提炼成要点。

sentences.en: There are also image generators that can create pictures from words, and many companies are using AI to automate tasks that used to need people, like answering customer questions or analyzing data.
sentences.zh: 还有能根据文字创作图片的图像生成器，许多公司正在使用AI来自动化那些原本需要人工来完成的任务，比如回答客户问题或分析数据。

sentences.en: Even driving cars. AI is becoming part of everyday life, I think.
sentences.zh: 甚至还能驾驶汽车。我想，AI正在成为日常生活的一部分。

sentences.en: AI is used in schools, hospitals, offices, entertainment.
sentences.zh: AI被广泛应用于学校、医院、办公室和娱乐领域。

sentences.en: At the same time, AI is growing very fast in business.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，AI在商业领域的增长也非常迅速。

sentences.en: Startups and new companies are appearing all over the world.
sentences.zh: 初创公司和新企业在世界各地不断涌现。

sentences.en: Some of these companies are reaching billion dollar valuations in just a few years.
sentences.zh: 其中一些公司在短短几年内估值就达到了数十亿美元。

sentences.en: This means investors think these companies are worth a lot of money, even if they’re not yet making big profits.
sentences.zh: 这意味着投资者认为这些公司价值不菲，即便它们目前还没有获得巨额利润。

sentences.en: In fact, the world’s most valuable company right now is currently Nvidia.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当今世界上最有价值的公司目前是Nvidia（英伟达）。

sentences.en: Nvidia is not directly an AI startup like Open AI or Anthropic, but it has become incredibly valuable due to the GPUs it creates, which are vital for AI systems to run.
sentences.zh: Nvidia并不是像Open AI或Anthropic那样直接的AI初创公司，但由于它生产的GPU对于AI系统的运行至关重要，因此变得极具价值。

sentences.en: Governments are also investing heavily in AI research and technology.
sentences.zh: 各国政府也在大力投资AI研发和技术。

sentences.en: So all of this growth and excitement creates a lot of attention and investment.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有这些增长和狂热吸引了大量的关注和投资。

sentences.en: People talk about AI as if it will change everything.
sentences.zh: 人们谈论AI时，仿佛它将改变一切。

sentences.en: It will change education, medicine, business, daily lives and more.
sentences.zh: 它将改变教育、医疗、商业、日常生活等等。

sentences.en: But is this growth real? Is this growth sustainable?
sentences.zh: 但这种增长是真实的吗？这种增长是可持续的吗？

sentences.en: Or is it like a bubble, where prices and expectations are higher than the real value?
sentences.zh: 还是说它就像一个泡沫，价格和期望远高于其实际价值？

sentences.en: Actually, we should probably define the term “bubble” in this context.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们或许应该在这个语境下定义“泡沫”这个词。

sentences.en: A bubble is a situation in economics or finance when the price of something, like houses or companies, becomes much higher than its real value.
sentences.zh: 泡沫是经济学或金融学中的一种现象，即某种事物（如房屋或公司）的价格远远高于其实际价值。

sentences.en: People pay more money than the thing is really worth because they expect the price to keep going up.
sentences.zh: 人们支付超出该事物真实价值的资金，是因为他们预期价格会持续上涨。

sentences.en: Bubbles usually happen when there is a lot of hype or excitement about a new opportunity.
sentences.zh: 泡沫通常发生在人们对新机遇充满炒作或狂热的时候。

sentences.en: People see others making money and they do not want to miss out.
sentences.zh: 人们看到别人赚钱，于是也按捺不住不想错过。

sentences.en: This feeling is now commonly called FOMO, the Fear Of Missing Out.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉现在通常被称为FOMO，即“错失恐惧症”。

sentences.en: There are some key features of a bubble.
sentences.zh: 泡沫有一些关键特征。

sentences.en: The first thing is speculation. This is where people speculate about the price, which means they form an idea or a theory based on guesses, without any real evidence.
sentences.zh: 首先是投机。这是指人们对价格进行投机，也就是说他们基于猜测形成某种想法或理论，而没有任何实际证据。

sentences.en: People buy something or invest in something because they expect the price to rise, not because of the real value.
sentences.zh: 人们买进某样东西或投资某样东西是因为他们期望价格上涨，而不是因为它的真实价值。

sentences.en: They are guessing that the price is going to be higher in the future.
sentences.zh: 他们在猜测未来价格会更高。

sentences.en: The next thing is overvaluation. Overvaluation means that the price goes far above the true value of the product or the company or the asset.
sentences.zh: 接下来是高估。高估意味着价格远高于产品、公司或资产的真实价值。

sentences.en: A good example of overvaluation is in the early days of the COVID pandemic, when things like antibacterial hand sanitizer and masks, which typically are quite cheap, were being sold for really high amounts of money.
sentences.zh: 高估的一个好例子是在新冠疫情初期，像抗菌洗手液和口罩这类通常很便宜的东西，却被以极高的价格售卖。

sentences.en: The next feature of a bubble is rapid growth.
sentences.zh: 泡沫的下一个特征是快速增长。

sentences.en: Prices increase quickly in a short time.
sentences.zh: 价格在短时间内迅速上涨。

sentences.en: And finally there is a sudden crash. Reality catches up.
sentences.zh: 最后是突然破裂。现实追赶了上来。

sentences.en: Prices fall very fast. And sometimes people lose a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 价格下跌得非常快。有时人们会损失大量的金钱。

sentences.en: Bubbles are not always bad. They often happen when new technology or new ideas excite people.
sentences.zh: 泡沫并不总是坏事。当新技术或新想法让人们兴奋时，它们往往就会出现。

sentences.en: Even if a bubble bursts, it can leave behind useful innovation, useful technology.
sentences.zh: 即使泡沫破裂，它也能留下有用的创新和有用的技术。

sentences.en: For example, the dot-com bubble in the early 2000s, which I’ll discuss very soon, caused many companies to fail, but the internet continued to grow and is now part of everyday life.
sentences.zh: 例如，2000年代初期的互联网泡沫（稍后我会讨论），导致许多公司倒闭，但互联网继续发展，现在已成为日常生活的一部分。

sentences.en: So in short, a bubble is a mix of hope, excitement, and too much optimism.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，泡沫是希望、狂热和过度乐观的混合体。

sentences.en: People believe something is more valuable than it really is, and this can create a risky situation.
sentences.zh: 人们相信某样东西比实际更有价值，这可能会造成一种危险的局面。

sentences.en: To understand whether AI could be a bubble, I think it would be helpful to look at some famous examples from history.
sentences.zh: 为了理解AI是否可能是一个泡沫，我认为回顾一下历史上的几个著名例子会很有帮助。

sentences.en: I’ll discuss three of the most famous historical bubbles, which show how bubbles start, grow, and eventually burst.
sentences.zh: 我将讨论三个最著名的历史泡沫，它们展示了泡沫是如何产生、发展并最终破裂的。

sentences.en: One of the earliest recorded financial bubbles is Tulip Mania, which occurred in the Netherlands during the 1630s.
sentences.zh: 有记录以来最早的金融泡沫之一是17世纪30年代发生在荷兰的“郁金香狂热”。

sentences.en: If you don’t know, a tulip is a type of flower.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道的话，郁金香是一种花卉。

sentences.en: In the 17th century, tulips were new to Europe.
sentences.zh: 在17世纪，郁金香对欧洲来说还是新鲜事物。

sentences.en: Their bright colors and unusual patterns made them extremely popular among wealthy people.
sentences.zh: 它们鲜艳的色彩和不寻常的花纹使它们在富人阶层中极为受欢迎。

sentences.en: Some tulips were rare or had broken colors caused by a virus, which made them even more desirable.
sentences.zh: 有些郁金香非常稀有，或者拥有由病毒引起的破色花纹，这使得它们更加抢手。

sentences.en: Initially, tulips were just a simple luxury flower for gardens, but speculation soon took over.
sentences.zh: 最初，郁金香只是花园里一种简单的奢侈花卉，但投机很快占了上风。

sentences.en: People began buying tulips to sell them for profit.
sentences.zh: 人们开始买卖郁金香以图利。

sentences.en: Prices started to rise rapidly. More people began to speculate on the price.
sentences.zh: 价格开始迅速上涨。越来越多的人开始对价格进行投机。

sentences.en: They would buy tulip bulbs with the hope or the idea that they would be able to sell them for more money in the future.
sentences.zh: 他们购买郁金香球茎，抱有的希望或想法是将来能把它们卖到更多的钱。

sentences.en: Ordinary people and merchants began investing their savings in tulips, believing the prices would continue to increase.
sentences.zh: 普通人和商人开始将积蓄投资于郁金香，坚信价格会持续上涨。

sentences.en: At the peak of tulip mania, some rare flowers were reportedly worth more than 10 times the annual income of a skilled worker and more than the price of a normal house.
sentences.zh: 在郁金香狂热的顶峰时期，据说一些稀有花卉的价值超过了一个熟练工人十年的收入，甚至超过了一栋普通房子的价格。

sentences.en: However, in 1637, the market collapsed. People realized that tulip bulbs had no value.
sentences.zh: 然而，到了1637年，市场崩溃了。人们意识到郁金香球茎根本没有价值。

sentences.en: They had no real value other than being a flower.
sentences.zh: 除了作为一朵花之外，它们没有任何真正的价值。

sentences.en: Buyers quickly disappeared and people who owned tulips, had invested their money, now just had some flowers dying in their store rooms.
sentences.zh: 买家迅速消失，那些拥有郁金香、投了资的人，现在手里只剩下一堆在储藏室里枯萎的花朵。

sentences.en: Prices fell dramatically. People were financially ruined.
sentences.zh: 价格急剧下跌。人们倾家荡产。

sentences.en: And actually the Dutch economy suffered a temporary shock.
sentences.zh: 事实上，荷兰经济也遭受了暂时的打击。

sentences.en: Another bubble happened in the 1990s and the early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 另一个泡沫发生在20世纪90年代和2000年代初。

sentences.en: We now call it the dot-com bubble. The dot-com bubble happened during the 1990s when the internet became widely available and widely popular.
sentences.zh: 我们现在称之为互联网泡沫。互联网泡沫发生在20世纪90年代，当时互联网开始普及并广受欢迎。

sentences.en: New technology companies, often called “dot-coms” because of their “. com” website addresses promised to revolutionize business, communication and shopping by using the internet.
sentences.zh: 新的科技公司通常被称为“网络公司”（dot-coms），因为它们的网址带有“.com”后缀，它们承诺通过使用互联网来彻底改变商业、通讯和购物。

sentences.en: This sounds obvious today, but in the 1990s and early 2000s, it was a new and exciting thing.
sentences.zh: 这在今天听起来显而易见，但在20世纪90年代和2000年代初，这是一件新鲜且令人兴奋的事情。

sentences.en: And investors were really eager to put money into internet companies.
sentences.zh: 投资者非常渴望将资金投入互联网公司。

sentences.en: They invested even if the company had no profits.
sentences.zh: 即使公司没有任何利润，他们也会进行投资。

sentences.en: Or actually had no product, in some cases.
sentences.zh: 或者在某些情况下，甚至根本没有产品。

sentences.en: Companies like pets.com became famous examples.
sentences.zh: 像pets.com这样的公司成为了著名的例子。

sentences.en: They raised millions of dollars from investors, even though their business models were unrealistic.
sentences.zh: 它们从投资者那里筹集了数百万美元，尽管它们的商业模式根本不切实际。

sentences.en: Pets.com was an early internet business in the USA that offered free shipping for items like dog food.
sentences.zh: Pets.com是美国早期的一家互联网企业，为狗粮等商品提供免费配送。

sentences.en: This was a terrible business model. They lost money on everything they sold because of the free shipping.
sentences.zh: 这是一个糟糕的商业模式。因为免费配送，他们卖出的每一样东西都在亏钱。

sentences.en: But the hype of the dot-com bubble led to pets.com becoming a public company in the year 2000.
sentences.zh: 但互联网泡沫的炒作让pets.com在2000年成为了一家上市公司。

sentences.en: They raised over $300 million from investors.
sentences.zh: 他们从投资者那里筹集了超过3亿美元。

sentences.en: Less than a year later, the company was bankrupt and gone.
sentences.zh: 不到一年后，该公司就宣告破产并消亡了。

sentences.en: In the dot-com bubble, stock prices of these tech companies rose rapidly, and people felt the fear of missing out.
sentences.zh: 在互联网泡沫期间，这些科技公司的股价迅速飙升，人们感受到了错失恐惧症。

sentences.en: They bought shares, they hoped the price would keep rising.
sentences.zh: 他们买入股票，希望价格能继续上涨。

sentences.en: At the peak of the bubble, many companies had market valuations far higher than the value of their actual business.
sentences.zh: 在泡沫顶峰时期，许多公司的市场估值远高于其实际业务的价值。

sentences.en: By 2000, reality began to catch up. Many companies failed and went bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 到2000年，现实开始显现。许多公司失败并破产。

sentences.en: The NASDAQ Stock Index, which included many tech companies, lost nearly 80% of its value.
sentences.zh: 纳斯达克股票指数包含了许多科技公司，其价值损失了近80%。

sentences.en: Millions of investors lost money, and the US economy entered a mild recession.
sentences.zh: 数百万投资者损失了金钱，美国经济进入了温和的衰退。

sentences.en: However, companies like Amazon, Google, and eBay survived.
sentences.zh: 然而，像亚马逊、谷歌和eBay这样的公司存活了下来。

sentences.en: They became profitable and eventually dominated the digital economy.
sentences.zh: 它们开始盈利，并最终主导了数字经济。

sentences.en: Even though the bubble burst, some valuable innovation remained and grew.
sentences.zh: 尽管泡沫破裂了，但一些有价值的创新得以保留并发展壮大。

sentences.en: The housing bubble of the 2000s is another recent and well-known example.
sentences.zh: 2000年代的房地产泡沫是另一个近期且广为人知的例子。

sentences.en: In the early 2000s, housing prices in the United States and other countries rose rapidly.
sentences.zh: 在2000年代初，美国和其他国家的房价迅速上涨。

sentences.en: Banks offered subprime mortgages, which were loans given to people with low or risky credit scores.
sentences.zh: 银行提供次级抵押贷款，即向信用评分低或有风险的人发放贷款。

sentences.en: These borrowers were expected to pay back more money than they could realistically afford.
sentences.zh: 这些借款人被认为需要偿还超出其现实承受能力的资金。

sentences.en: Basically, the banks were giving people mortgages, loans, who couldn’t afford those loans.
sentences.zh: 基本上，银行在向那些根本买不起房的人发放抵押贷款。

sentences.en: Many people used this money to buy houses as investments.
sentences.zh: 许多人利用这笔资金买房作为投资。

sentences.en: They believed that property values would always rise, houses would always become more expensive.
sentences.zh: 他们坚信房地产价值永远会上涨，房子只会越来越贵。

sentences.en: Financial institutions also created complex financial products called mortgage backed securities, which basically bundled many risky loans together and then sold them.
sentences.zh: 金融机构还创造了被称为抵押贷款支持证券的复杂金融产品，这基本上是将许多高风险贷款捆绑在一起然后出售。

sentences.en: Investors around the world bought these securities believing they were safe.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的投资者买入这些证券，认为它们是安全的。

sentences.en: By 2007, the bubble had grown very large.
sentences.zh: 到2007年，泡沫已经变得非常巨大。

sentences.en: Eventually, too many homeowners could not pay their loans, and the housing market began to collapse.
sentences.zh: 最终，太多的房主无力偿还贷款，房地产市场开始崩盘。

sentences.en: Prices fell sharply. Banks failed or needed government bailouts.
sentences.zh: 价格急剧下跌。银行倒闭或需要政府救助。

sentences.en: And the world entered a financial crisis in 2008.
sentences.zh: 世界在2008年陷入了金融危机。

sentences.en: Millions of people lost their jobs, lost their savings, and lost their homes.
sentences.zh: 数百万的人失去了工作、积蓄和家园。

sentences.en: So now we have looked at those examples of past bubbles, is AI a bubble?
sentences.zh: 那么，在我们回顾了过去这些泡沫的例子之后，AI是一个泡沫吗？

sentences.en: The valuation of many businesses connected to AI are skyrocketing.
sentences.zh: 许多与AI相关的企业的估值正在飙升。

sentences.en: I mentioned Nvidia earlier in this episode, which is now the most valuable company in the world.
sentences.zh: 我在本期节目的早些时候提到了Nvidia，它现在是世界上最有价值的公司。

sentences.en: Many AI startups are also reaching billion dollar valuations.
sentences.zh: 许多AI初创公司的估值也在达到数十亿美元。

sentences.en: However, there is a problem with many AI startups.
sentences.zh: 然而，许多AI初创公司存在一个问题。

sentences.en: They’re not making money. Many are not making significant profits.
sentences.zh: 它们不赚钱。许多公司没有产生可观的利润。

sentences.en: They’re losing money. Investors right now are paying for future potential rather than real results.
sentences.zh: 它们在亏损。现在的投资者为未来的潜力买单，而不是为实际结果买单。

sentences.en: Just like in historical bubbles, there is a lot of hype.
sentences.zh: 就像历史上的泡沫一样，这里有大量的炒作。

sentences.en: Media headlines suggest AI is going to change everything, and people fear missing out, which leads to more investment.
sentences.zh: 媒体的头条新闻暗示AI将改变一切，人们害怕错过，这导致了更多的投资。

sentences.en: I think there are also some unrealistic expectations about AI.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对AI也存在一些不切实际的期望。

sentences.en: Some companies and investors overstate the capabilities of AI.
sentences.zh: 一些公司和投资者夸大了AI的能力。

sentences.en: Now, we all know AI is powerful, but it’s not perfect.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们都知道AI很强大，但它并不完美。

sentences.en: It may become better in the future or it may not.
sentences.zh: 它未来可能会变得更好，也可能不会。

sentences.en: Overconfidence can create this imbalance where the perceived value and the actual value are different.
sentences.zh: 过度自信会造成这种失衡，即感知价值与实际价值存在差异。

sentences.en: And while AI is expanding quickly, some models are very expensive to train and run.
sentences.zh: 虽然AI正在迅速扩张，但某些模型的训练和运行成本非常高昂。

sentences.en: And not every AI application will generate a profit.
sentences.zh: 并非每个AI应用都能产生利润。

sentences.en: This situation is similar to the dot-com companies that had huge hype but no solid revenue.
sentences.zh: 这种情况类似于那些炒作巨大却没有稳定收入的网络公司。

sentences.en: I think some companies that exist now will definitely become massive and successful giant corporations like the survivors from the dot-com bubble, maybe Google and Amazon.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在存在的一些公司未来绝对会成长为庞大且成功的巨无霸企业，就像互联网泡沫中的幸存者那样，比如谷歌和亚马逊。

sentences.en: But it’s also likely some of these startups will be more similar to pets.com.
sentences.zh: 但其中一些初创公司也很有可能更类似于pets.com。

sentences.en: However, there are of course people who believe AI is not a bubble.
sentences.zh: 然而，当然也有人认为AI不是泡沫。

sentences.en: Unlike past bubbles, AI is already solving real problems.
sentences.zh: 与过去的泡沫不同，AI已经在解决实际问题。

sentences.en: It’s used in medicine, translation, customer service, research, and creative industries.
sentences.zh: 它被用于医学、翻译、客户服务、研究和创意产业。

sentences.en: The transcript for this episode you are listening to right now is created using AI technology.
sentences.zh: 你现在正在收听的本期节目的字幕就是使用AI技术创建的。

sentences.en: It’s not like a tulip bulb from the 1700s, AI is actually a useful thing.
sentences.zh: 它不像1700年代的郁金香球茎，AI确实是一个有用的东西。

sentences.en: Governments and large corporations are also building systems and platforms based on AI.
sentences.zh: 政府和大型企业也在构建基于AI的系统和平台。

sentences.en: I think this suggests some long-term investment rather than short term speculation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这表明这是一种长期投资，而不是短期投机。

sentences.en: And even if some AI companies fail and some will fail, the technology will continue to grow just as the internet survived the dot-com bubble.
sentences.zh: 即使一些AI公司会倒闭（确实会有一部分倒闭），这项技术也将继续发展，就像互联网在互联网泡沫中存活下来一样。

sentences.en: So, if AI is in a bubble, what could happen if it bursts?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果AI正处于泡沫之中，如果它破裂了会发生什么？

sentences.en: A burst bubble happens when prices, investments, or expectations suddenly fall.
sentences.zh: 泡沫破裂发生在价格、投资或预期突然下跌的时候。

sentences.en: And reality no longer matches the hype. And as we saw earlier in this episode, burst bubbles can have serious consequences.
sentences.zh: 现实不再符合炒作。正如我们在本期节目早些时候所看到的，泡沫破裂会产生严重的后果。

sentences.en: People who invested in overvalued AI companies could see their investments drop sharply in value.
sentences.zh: 投资于被高估的AI公司的投资者会看到他们的投资价值急剧下降。

sentences.en: As we saw with the dot-com bubble, this could also mean a collapse in the value of stock exchanges as well as individual companies.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在互联网泡沫中看到的那样，这也可能意味着证券交易所及个别公司价值的崩溃。

sentences.en: So this doesn’t just affect people investing directly in the company, but also people who maybe their pension is tracked along to a stock exchange.
sentences.zh: 因此，这不仅影响直接投资于该公司的人，还影响那些可能把养老金与证券交易所挂钩的人。

sentences.en: If the stock exchange falls, so does your pension.
sentences.zh: 如果股市下跌，你的养老金也会缩水。

sentences.en: Startups or even larger companies that rely on this hype rather than solid business models probably will go bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 依赖这种炒作而不是扎实商业模型的初创公司甚至规模更大的公司可能会破产。

sentences.en: And if companies fail, then workers will lose their jobs.
sentences.zh: 如果公司倒闭，那么工人就会失业。

sentences.en: There is also a risk that too much money is being invested in AI and not enough in other useful areas.
sentences.zh: 还有一个风险是，太多的资金被投入到AI中，而投入到其他有用领域的资金不足。

sentences.en: Money might go to these trendy AI projects instead of practical solutions or better technology.
sentences.zh: 资金可能会流向这些赶时髦的AI项目，而不是实用的解决方案或更好的技术。

sentences.en: Some AI products will fail to meet our expectations, and companies may choose to use the label “AI powered” for hype rather than true technological advancement.
sentences.zh: 一些AI产品将无法达到我们的预期，公司可能会为了炒作而选择使用“AI驱动”的标签，而不是真正的技术进步。

sentences.en: If AI does not meet people’s high expectations, then our trust in the technology could decrease.
sentences.zh: 如果AI没有达到人们的高期望，那么我们对这项技术的信任可能会下降。

sentences.en: Overhyped claims can create fear about AI taking jobs or making decisions, even when the technology is not yet able to do that.
sentences.zh: 过度炒作的言论可能会引起人们对AI抢走工作或做出决策的恐惧，尽管这项技术目前还无法做到这一点。

sentences.en: And governments may delay some regulation because of overconfidence or panic after a bubble bursts.
sentences.zh: 在泡沫破裂后，由于过度自信或恐慌，政府可能会推迟某些监管。

sentences.en: However, even when bubbles burst, not everything is lost.
sentences.zh: 然而，即使泡沫破裂，也并非一切都失去了。

sentences.en: Just like the internet survived the dot-com bubble, AI could continue to grow and improve.
sentences.zh: 就像互联网在互联网泡沫中存活下来一样，AI可以继续成长和完善。

sentences.en: The key difference is that today AI already has real applications and real value, which I think could make it more resilient than past bubbles.
sentences.zh: 关键区别在于，今天的AI已经有了实际的应用和真正的价值，我认为这可能使其比过去的泡沫更具韧性。

sentences.en: We have explored the idea of a “bubble” in this episode, looking at history and asking whether AI might be in one.
sentences.zh: 我们在本期节目中探讨了“泡沫”的概念，回顾了历史，并询问AI是否正身处其中。

sentences.en: A bubble happens when people expect more value than something actually has.
sentences.zh: 当人们对某事物的期望值超过其实际价值时，泡沫就产生了。

sentences.en: Bubbles are driven by excitement, speculation, and sometimes the fear of missing out.
sentences.zh: 泡沫是由兴奋、投机以及有时对错失恐惧的心理驱动的。

sentences.en: History shows us that bubbles can be risky, but they often leave behind innovation and new technology.
sentences.zh: 历史告诉我们，泡沫可能具有风险，但它们往往会留下创新和新技术。

sentences.en: When it comes to AI, the picture is mixed.
sentences.zh: 说到AI，情况则比较复杂。

sentences.en: There are signs of hype and overvaluation, which is very typical of bubbles.
sentences.zh: 有迹象表明存在炒作和估值过高，这非常符合泡沫的典型特征。

sentences.en: At the same time, AI already has real value.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，AI已经具备了实际价值。

sentences.en: It’s solving problems in medicine and business, education and entertainment.
sentences.zh: 它正在解决医学、商业、教育和娱乐领域的问题。

sentences.en: Even if some AI companies fail, I think the technology itself will likely continue to grow and change the world.
sentences.zh: 即使一些AI公司失败了，我认为这项技术本身很可能会继续发展并改变世界。

sentences.en: But what do you think? Is AI a bubble? How can we use AI responsibly?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？AI是一个泡沫吗？我们该如何负责任地使用AI？
